facts.fact: 叙述者在早餐室自取香肠、吐司、橙汁、水波蛋和培根，独自吃了半个小时
facts.anchor: I helped myself to sausages and toast, fresh orange juice, poached eggs, and bacon.

facts.fact: 仆人关注地看着她添第二第三次餐，既不讥笑也不责备
facts.anchor: The servants watched attentively as I went back for second and third helpings but didn’t smirk or scold.

facts.fact: 邻桌穿灰西装的年轻丈夫只剩一只手，妻子替他点烟——又一名战争伤员
facts.anchor: When his wife lit a cigarette for him, I saw he had only one hand.

facts.fact: 面对独坐金发女人的打量，叙述者低头认输般离开了早餐室
facts.anchor: I lowered my head, knowing this small gesture would be read as a capitulation.

facts.fact: 叙述者在陈列柜抽屉里看到茧、蛹与卵，标本上还留着毒瓶的气味
facts.anchor: The faint grassy scent of the killing jar still clung to them.

facts.fact: 画廊里全是旧大师名作，Miss Irikos 既敬重又鄙夷他们，因为其中没有女性
facts.anchor: There were paintings here by great artists—the old masters Miss Irikos had both revered and disdained, because there were no women among them.

facts.fact: 叙述者凑近看画上签名是 Meredith Kalman，倒吸一口气，觉得这更像梦魇而非梦
facts.anchor: Meredith Kalman. I sucked in my breath.

facts.fact: 画廊扶手椅里的男人起身走向她，正是杂志报刊照片上认得的 Rex de Voil
facts.anchor: his face recognizable from magazine and newspaper photographs: Rex de Voil.
